lines: Air pushes slowly through the ductwork, cold and tasting of rust.
A long breath of wind slides down the shaft and dies out.
Sheet metal ticks as the duct cools in the dark.
The grille above you rattles once, then holds still.
Something drags across the ceiling panels, slow and deliberate.
A hatch bangs open somewhere in the ducts, then slams shut.
Air hisses through a seam in the ventilation line.
The fan behind the grate coughs and picks up speed.
Thin dust sifts through the grille and settles on your sleeve.
Metal ribs in the duct creak as the temperature drops.
A rolling clank travels along the duct and fades.
The air stirs warm, then goes cold again without warning.
Somewhere in the ceiling, a panel shifts with a dry scrape.
The draft pulls at your hair and smells of wet concrete.
Louvres flutter against each other in the moving air.
A tin lid bounces down the duct and rattles to a stop.
Three light taps sound on the sheet metal overhead.
The ventilation hum swells, then drops to a low murmur.
Ducts ring faintly as the building exhales through them.
A damper clicks shut far up the line, sealing the route.
Grit patters down through the grille like sleet.
No draft comes through the grate, though the metal still hums.
Scorched oil rides a warm gust up out of the vent.
Sheet metal pops as the heat leaves the ductwork.
A heavy weight shifts in the duct, and the walls boom faintly.
The gap under the door whistles as the draft finds it.
A long, uneven whistle leaks out through the grille.
A bolt drops somewhere in the ducts and rolls away.
Each gust through the shaft rattles the louvres a little harder.
Overhead, a plate knocks against its frame and falls quiet.
Air hums through the line like someone blowing over a bottle.
The duct ticks, pauses, then ticks again closer.
A muffled bang rolls through the ceiling and into the room.
Fine ash drifts from the grate and dusts the floor.
The vent cover hums up a note, then slides back down.
Taps walk along the duct, slow and patient, one at a time.
A hatch lid clangs shut two rooms over.
The draft carries a faint smell of machine oil and rain.
Wind pushes up the shaft and the whole grille shivers.
Pipes and ducts settle together, sighing in the dark.
Scraping runs along the ductwork above the ceiling tiles.
Loose in its frame, the grille clatters, then clicks home.
Cool air rushes out of the ceiling and then stops dead.
Sheet metal sings softly when the air changes speed.
A soft thud comes from inside the wall, then nothing.
The exhaust fan wheezes, catches, and starts up again.
Dust swirls in the light coming through the louvres.
A loose panel bangs in the duct and echoes down the line.
The shaft breathes out a long, low note.
Heat shimmers off the grate, and the metal creaks.
A can rolls slowly along the ducts overhead, then stops.
A thread of cold air touches your neck from the buzzing grille.
Faint scratching moves across the ceiling, going left.
A hatch somewhere above swings on a rusted hinge.
The fan blades tick against the housing with each turn.
Gusts race down the duct, then drop to nothing at once.
Wet drips patter down a duct wall in a slow rhythm.
Metal clanks twice in the ceiling, then stays silent.
Vents hiss in turn down the length of the corridor.
Slow weight creaks a ceiling grille, then lifts away.
The draft changes direction, and the dust follows it.
The ductwork knocks once, then waits, as if listening back.
The air sighs out of a broken louvre near the floor.
Old sheet metal groans as the pressure builds behind it.
A dull drumming runs through the ceiling, then stops abruptly.
The grate hums and the lamp above it flickers.
Cold air pours from a torn seam in the duct.
The ventilation line clicks as the fan slows to a stop.
Ceiling tiles shiver as something passes over them.
Air moves through the ducts in long, uneven gusts.
A metal flap bangs on its hinge, twice, then holds.
Grit rattles down the shaft and pings off the grille.
The duct's metal skin ticks and expands in the heat.
A knock comes from the far side of the grille, then withdraws.
Stale air drifts down through the grille, thick with dust.
